jobs.description:
AD Group (Australia) Pty Ltd
is looking for Technical Project Manager

Key Points

Work closely with experienced engineering teams across multiple software platforms and products.
Remote working environment.
Regular collaboration with Australian teams and stakeholders.
Holidays on Australian Federal holidays.

Job Description / Responsibility

Project and Delivery Management

Manage software projects and development work from initial planning through to release.
Coordinate work across backend, frontend, QA, DevOps, integrations and other technical areas.
Ensure requirements are properly understood and broken down before development begins.
Maintain clear delivery plans, priorities, dependencies and timelines.
Identify blockers, risks and dependencies early and work with the relevant people to resolve them.
Track delivery progress and ensure agreed actions are followed through.
Help teams maintain realistic commitments rather than allowing work to drift between sprints.
Support release planning and ensure development, testing and deployment activities are coordinated.

Agile and Engineering Process

Facilitate sprint planning, backlog refinement, stand ups, retrospectives and other delivery discussions where required.
Keep Jira boards, tickets, priorities, dependencies and delivery information accurate and useful.
Ensure tickets contain sufficient business and technical context before development starts.
Work with technical leads to make sure larger work is appropriately broken down.
Help ensure engineering processes are followed consistently.
Improve delivery processes where existing practices are creating unnecessary delays or confusion.
Focus on practical delivery outcomes rather than applying Agile or Scrum processes mechanically.

Technical Understanding

Backend and frontend development
APIs and third party integrations
Databases and data flows
Cloud infrastructure and deployment processes
QA, regression testing and release management
Software architecture and technical dependencies

Stakeholder Communication

Strong English communication is a critical requirement for this role.

You will regularly communicate directly with Australian stakeholders, engineering leadership and other teams.
You must be able to:
Communicate confidently and professionally in spoken English.
Write clear and concise updates in English.
Explain technical issues to non technical stakeholders.
Provide simple and accurate project status updates.
Escalate risks early rather than waiting until deadlines are missed.
Manage expectations professionally when timelines or requirements change.
Lead meetings confidently and keep discussions focused on decisions and actions.

Clear communication matters

We particularly value people who can explain: what happened, the impact, what is being done, who owns the next action and when the issue is expected to be resolved.

Bachelor/Honors

Experience Requirements

At least 5 year(s)
The applicants should have experience in the following business area(s):Software Company

Approximately 5+ years of professional experience within software or technology environments.
At least 3 years of experience in technical project management, software delivery, Scrum Master, delivery management or a similar role.
Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle.
Experience managing software engineering teams or coordinating complex software projects.
Experience with Agile development practices.
Strong Jira or similar project management tool experience.
Experience coordinating developers, QA engineers and technical leads.
Strong spoken and written English.
Experience communicating directly with international clients or stakeholders.
Strong organizational and prioritization skills.
Ability to manage several workstreams at the same time.
Strong problem solving and decision making capability.

Anywhere in Bangladesh

Tk. 200000 - 400000 (Monthly)

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
2-Year Fixed Term Contract
Brisbane preferred | Sydney, Melbourne or Canberra considered
Deliver major infrastructure and construction projects across Australia's airport network

Summary

Join Airservices Australia's ARFFS NexGen Program and play a key role in delivering critical infrastructure projects that support Aviation Rescue Fire Fighting Services (ARFFS) across Australia.

As a Senior Project Manager, you will lead a portfolio of construction and infrastructure projects across the Eastern region, managing the delivery of new facilities, upgrades and associated infrastructure works from planning and design through to construction, commissioning and operational handover.

Working within a collaborative and highly capable team, you'll partner with contractors, consultants and operational stakeholders to deliver projects that directly support the future of aviation safety and emergency response capabilities nationwide.

The Organisation

Airservices Australia is a government-owned organisation responsible for the safe and efficient management of 11% of the world's airspace and the provision of aviation rescue fire fighting services at Australia's busiest airports.

Our people are our greatest asset, with a dynamic and diverse workforce operating across metropolitan, regional and remote locations throughout Australia. Together, we help connect people safely with their world while supporting economic growth, trade and tourism.

Airservices is committed to fostering a culture that is diverse, inclusive and respectful. We encourage motivated individuals who value collaboration, accountability and service excellence to explore a career with Airservices.

The Role & The Team

As a Senior Project Manager within the ARFFS NexGen Program, you will be responsible for leading multiple concurrent infrastructure and construction projects across Airservices' Eastern Region portfolio.

You will oversee all phases of project delivery, including planning, design management, procurement, tendering, contractor engagement, construction delivery, commissioning and project close-out. Working across a geographically dispersed stakeholder network, you will ensure projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and in line with operational requirements.

This role forms part of a close-knit and experienced project team that values collaboration, transparency and practical problem-solving. You will have the opportunity to contribute to nationally significant infrastructure programs while working alongside project professionals delivering complex outcomes across the Airservices network.

Key Responsibilities Include

Managing the end-to-end delivery of construction and infrastructure projects.
Developing and maintaining project plans, schedules, budgets and governance requirements.
Managing consultants, contractors and delivery partners.
Monitoring project performance, risks, issues and project dependencies.
Building strong relationships with operational, technical and executive stakeholders.
Supporting the successful delivery of ARFFS NexGen and associated infrastructure initiatives.
Driving safe project delivery outcomes and compliance with organisational governance frameworks.

Please see the Position Description below for further information regarding the role and responsibilities.

The Person

You are an experienced project professional with strong construction and infrastructure delivery expertise. You enjoy working in complex stakeholder environments and have a proven ability to lead projects from concept through to operational handover.

You are commercially astute, outcomes-focused and comfortable managing competing priorities while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality and delivery excellence.

The Successful Applicant Will Demonstrate

Significant experience delivering complex construction, infrastructure, facilities or capital works projects.
Strong contractor, consultant and contract management capability.
Experience managing project governance, schedules, budgets, risk and reporting.
Proven ability to lead multiple projects concurrently across different locations.
Highly developed stakeholder engagement and influencing skills.
Strong commercial and financial management experience.
Experience operating within government, aviation, transport, utilities, critical infrastructure or similarly regulated environments will be highly regarded.
Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline.

At Airservices Australia, we embrace and thrive on diversity of thought, perspectives and capabilities because we know the benefits of having a workforce that is representative of the community we serve.

We believe a diverse workforce supported by an inclusive culture is central to our success. We actively encourage and welcome candidates from all cultural backgrounds, gender identities, people living with disability, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply.

Security Clearance

To be eligible to apply, you must be an Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident, as an ASIC may be required for this role.

How To Apply

To apply for this position please lodge an application online before 11:55pm (AEST) Thursday 29th October 2026.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Strategic Operations Manager based in the United States.

This is an exciting opportunity for a data-driven operations professional to help a growing organization scale efficiently and make smarter, evidence-based decisions. Reporting to the Director of Strategic Operations, you will combine analytical expertise with project leadership to transform business insights into measurable operational improvements. You will investigate performance trends, build dashboards, and identify opportunities to optimize workflows across multiple departments. The role involves leading complex initiatives from planning through execution while aligning stakeholders around clear goals, timelines, and deliverables. You will work in a collaborative, fast-paced, and remote-first environment where curiosity, ownership, and adaptability are highly valued. This position offers the opportunity to influence strategic decisions, improve operational performance, and contribute to the evolution of technology-enabled legal services.

Accountabilities

Analyze operational data to uncover trends, investigate performance variations, identify inefficiencies, and answer critical business questions.
Own the process of generating operational insights and following through on recommendations, ensuring that analysis translates into concrete actions and measurable business outcomes.
Develop, maintain, and improve dashboards and reporting tools that communicate operational performance clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Lead complex operational projects from initial scoping and planning through implementation and completion, establishing clear objectives, timelines, deliverables, and accountability.
Coordinate cross-functional initiatives involving multiple departments and stakeholders, ensuring effective communication, alignment, and progress toward shared goals.
Translate analytical findings into structured improvement initiatives with defined success metrics, actionable recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
Identify opportunities to streamline processes, eliminate inefficiencies, and design and implement new workflows that improve operational effectiveness.
Facilitate meetings, workshops, and strategic planning sessions to gather insights, resolve challenges, align priorities, and drive decision-making.
Present analytical findings, project updates, and recommendations to stakeholders at all organizational levels, adapting communication to different audiences.
Proactively anticipate business needs through data analysis, performance monitoring, and forward-looking project planning.
Partner closely with the Director of Strategic Operations to coordinate multiple initiatives, extend operational leadership capacity, and support strategic priorities.
Manage competing deadlines and evolving business requirements while maintaining high standards of analytical rigor, project execution, and communication.
Identify opportunities to improve reporting processes, data accessibility, and operational decision-making through business intelligence tools and emerging analytical techniques.

Requirements

Three to five years of professional experience combining data analytics and project management, ideally within a high-growth startup, financial institution, consulting firm, or similarly fast-paced organization.
Advanced proficiency in data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using tools such as Microsoft Excel, Looker, and Tableau.
Strong SQL skills and familiarity with modern business intelligence (BI) tools, particularly for querying datasets, building dashboards, and translating complex information into actionable insights.
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional projects and coordinating stakeholders across multiple departments, with a track record of delivering initiatives successfully.
Strong organizational and project management skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities, establish timelines, track deliverables, and maintain accountability.
Highly developed analytical thinking and intellectual curiosity, with the ability to investigate complex problems, challenge assumptions, identify patterns, and develop evidence-based solutions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain analytical findings and technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
A proactive, self-directed approach to work, with the ability to identify opportunities, make sound decisions, and deliver results with limited supervision.
Comfort working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment characterized by ambiguity, changing priorities, and evolving business needs.
Strong attention to detail and a practical, results-oriented mindset, with the ability to connect data analysis to operational execution and business impact.
Experience with Snowflake, dbt, Fivetran, Python, or R is an advantage.
Familiarity with machine learning concepts, legal technology, professional services, or operational teams within complex, service-based businesses is preferred.
Ability to work effectively in a remote environment, collaborating with distributed teams and maintaining clear communication across stakeholders.

Benefits

Remote work: A fully remote position based in the United States.
Flexible scheduling: A flexible work environment that supports autonomy, productivity, and work-life balance.

Comprehensive healthcare: Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage, with options for employees and their families. Some plans include 100% premium coverage.

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota is hiring a Program Manager, Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality. In this position, you’ll be responsible for the design, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing management of the Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality Program, supporting Medicare, Medicaid, ACA, and Commercial populations to optimize Blue Cross’s earned risk-adjusted revenue. The role serves as the subject matter expert for risk adjustment coding, partnering with leadership and cross-functional teams to develop and execute strategic initiatives, identify data trends, and implement performance improvement opportunities through collaboration with analytics and other key stakeholders. jobs.title: Senior / Physical Security Manager
jobs.description:
Purpose of the role:

Lead and manage the Bank's physical security operations across its branch, office and critical-facility portfolio. The role covers physical security governance, guarding services, CCTV surveillance, premises access control, incident management, security risk assessment and operational resilience. The position is responsible for developing and implementing appropriate policies, standards, processes and risk-mitigation measures to protect employees, customers, premises, assets and business operations, while ensuring alignment with OCBC Group requirements and applicable local regulatory expectations.

What you will be doing:
1. Security Operations Management
Manage physical security operations across the Bank's branches, offices and other relevant premises, including guarding, CCTV surveillance, access control and alarm monitoring.
Develop and maintain a centralised security management framework, operating procedures and reporting mechanisms to support business and operational requirements.
Ensure the Security Command Centre provides timely monitoring, escalation and response to security incidents.

2. Governance, Policy and Compliance
Own and maintain OCBC Hong Kong physical security policies, standards and procedures in alignment with OCBC Group requirements.
Ensure security operations comply with applicable internal policies, approval authorities, audit requirements and local regulatory expectations.
Coordinate and support internal reviews, audits, control testing and remediation of identified security gaps.

3. Physical Security Risk Management
Conduct or coordinate periodic physical security assessments, including threat and vulnerability risk assessments, for branches, offices and critical facilities.
Review security risks associated with new premises, renovation projects, relocation exercises and changes in business operations, and recommend appropriate controls.
Provide physical security advisory support to business units and review risk acceptance or control exceptions in accordance with established governance.

4. Incident, Crisis and Operational Resilience
Lead or support the response, investigation, escalation and reporting of physical security incidents.
Prepare clear incident reports, identify root causes and ensure corrective and preventive actions are tracked to completion.
Support crisis management, business continuity and operational resilience planning, including emergency drills and scenario exercises relating to physical security threats.

5. Projects and Workplace Transformation
Work closely with Property Services, project teams, building management and business representatives to define and deliver physical security requirements for office and branch projects.
Support Project Helix, OCC Tower and other workplace transformation, relocation, fit-out or renovation initiatives by establishing security design requirements and ensuring proper testing, commissioning and handover.
Organise project and stakeholder meetings to confirm operational requirements, resolve security issues and monitor implementation progress.

6. Security Systems and Technology
Oversee lifecycle management, maintenance and enhancement of CCTV, access control, intrusion detection and related security platforms and equipment.
Drive appropriate technology upgrades, system integration and process digitalisation to strengthen monitoring capability, reliability and operational efficiency.
Maintain appropriate system documentation, access administration, testing records and business continuity arrangements for critical security systems.

7. Vendor and Contract Management
Manage security guarding providers, system vendors and other third-party security service providers, including service performance, contract governance and cost control.
Define and monitor service levels and key performance indicators, and ensure timely remediation of service deficiencies.
Assess the adequacy of third-party physical security controls and ensure compliance with the Bank's security and vendor-management requirements.

8. Continuous Improvement and Other Duties
Monitor the physical security threat landscape and recommend proportionate improvements to security controls, processes and services.
Prepare management information, performance reports, risk updates and recommendations for senior management and relevant governance forums.
Perform ad-hoc assignments and projects as required.

Who are we looking for:

Degree or professional qualification in security management, risk management, facilities management, engineering or related discipline.
Relevant experience in physical security operations, preferably within banking, financial services, a regulated environment or a large multi-site organisation.
Practical experience in CCTV, access control, guarding operations, incident management, security risk assessment and vendor management.
Experience supporting office, branch, fit-out, relocation or workplace transformation projects.
Professional certifications in security, risk, business continuity or project management are advantageous.

About the role

The Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst supports security and risk decisions across one Of the world's largest cloud and technology environments. We identify, assess, and communicate threats, vulnerabilities, and emerging risks that could impact critical infrastructure, personnel, operations, supply chains, and strategic business initiatives. The successful candidate will operate at the intersection of intelligence collection, investigations, risk management technical analysis, and stakeholder engagement. This is not a traditional security operations or monitoring role. We are seeking an individual who can independently identify leads, develop investigative hypotheses, conduct collection activities, analyze complex information, and drive issues to resolution through persistence, curiosity, and critical thinking.

What you'll do

This role provides the opportunity to work on complex, high-impact security challenges within a global technology environment supporting some of the world's most advanced cloud and Al initiatives. Analysts are exposed to a wide range of missions including intelligence collection, investigations, insider threat supply chain risk, emerging technologies, strategic vulnerability assessments, and geopolitical risk analysis. Team members regularly collaborate with experienced professionals across intelligence, cybersecurity, engineering, investigations, legal, compliance, risk management and physical security disciplines. This position offers exceptional opportunities for professional growth, technical development cross-functional engagement, and exposure to some of the most challenging security and intelligence problems in the industry.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add.

We're Looking For a Technical Program Manager To Drive The Programs That Scale It. The Work Spans Four Closely Coupled Areas

Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online.
Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform.
Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request.
Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance.

This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like.

Key Responsibilities

Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery.
Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path.
Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision.
Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps.
Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org.
Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams.
Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion.
Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs.

Minimum Qualifications

7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it.
Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking.
A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly.
A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep.
The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers.
Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on.
Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit.
Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing.
Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform.
Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services.
Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity.
Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work.
Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling.
Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements.
Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$290,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. jobs.title: Staff Program Manager, Event Design
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

Brand Studio lays the foundations that help Stripe accelerate. We do this by creating, evolving, and maintaining Stripe’s high-quality, versatile, and forward-looking brand design systems, experiences, and advertising campaigns. We sweat the details. We make it seem effortless.

What you’ll do

You will be responsible for leading brand design operations and creative production across all of Stripe’s internal and external events, in close partnership with the Experiential Creative Director. This role is a hybrid mix of program management, project management, and creative production depending on the project phase. During certain periods you’ll be focused on the 10,000 foot view of the program, and at other times you’ll be working side-by-side with the Design team overseeing execution of every design detail before an event.

Responsibilities

Lead experiential program management across roadmap development, budget oversight, project scoping, timelines, resourcing, partner relationships, cross-functional communication, and scalable approaches that create clear paths forward
Manage a high volume of simultaneous projects, ranging from small to large scale
Partner closely with the Experiential Creative Director to further scale and evolve event design at Stripe; optimize processes to streamline how work is done
Partner closely with the Corporate Events team to ensure smooth execution and integration of event brand design across all surfaces
Ensure smooth collaboration with leadership, creatives, cross-functional partners, and vendors
Own project management through documentation, tooling, trackers, standing meetings, org-wide updates, and Slack
Source, onboard, and oversee external creative agencies
Connect silos, socialize changes, anticipate risks, and provide actionable solutions for escalation to Brand Studio leadership
Navigate challenges and blockers with ease; proactive in finding solutions, and always looking ahead for the team
Uphold and advocate for design quality with cross-functional teams and vendors to exceed engagement and registration goals
Inspire and sustain a culture of excellence by collaborating with creatives in best practices and processes

Who you are

Staff Program Managers within Brand Studio at Stripe demonstrate passion for great design and have strong design sense. They’re experts in diving deep into details, expanding, evolving, defining, and documenting flexible systems and processes that achieve bar-raising quality and consistency at scale.

The ideal candidate excels at keeping the work on track while maintaining (and raising) the bar on craft. They offer options and tradeoffs, crisply articulate decisions, iterate quickly, and collaborate seamlessly with senior leadership, marketers, creatives, and agency partners. Most importantly, they are meticulous when it comes to details.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in similar roles and industries
Think users first—understand their needs, find interesting and unique solutions, and strive to consistently optimize how to best engage with them
Have a strong strategic acumen for developing complex program roadmaps and cross-functional processes in a fast-paced environment
Can demonstrate strong design sense, industry knowledge and best practices, have deep knowledge producing complex brand and event design systems, and bringing design assets to life across the creative production process
Proven excellence in producing creative systems that are optimized for scale and growth
Highly detail oriented and excel at simplifying complexity
Strong track record successfully influencing outcomes both internally and with agency partners
Can balance optimizing for speed and quality, with high craft and quality creative work
Are persuasive in explaining your work, process, and decisions
Excellent organization and presentation skills, and excel in written and verbal communication
Are passionate about Stripe’s mission

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,000 - $276,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

About Blue Cross And Blue Shield Of Minnesota

At Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, we are committed to paving the way for everyone to achieve their healthiest life. We are looking for dedicated and motivated individuals who share our vision of transforming healthcare. As a Blue Cross associate, you are joining a culture that is built on values of succeeding together, finding a better way, and doing the right thing. If you are ready to make a difference, join us.

The Impact You Will Have

Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota is hiring a Program Manager, Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality. In this position, you’ll be responsible for the design, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing management of the Risk Adjustment Coding and Quality Program, supporting Medicare, Medicaid, ACA, and Commercial populations to optimize Blue Cross’s earned risk-adjusted revenue. The role serves as the subject matter expert for risk adjustment coding, partnering with leadership and cross-functional teams to develop and execute strategic initiatives, identify data trends, and implement performance improvement opportunities through collaboration with analytics and other key stakeholders. The incumbent ensures program strategies and operations meet evolving regulatory, market, provider, and member requirements while addressing complex business challenges and supporting organizational change. Acting as a liaison across multiple departments, the individual leads enterprise-wide initiatives, drives results within established timelines, and provides leadership and oversight to program management staff within the division. Working closely with the Director, this position supports the implementation of strategic initiatives, monitors project progress, and oversees team and vendor performance to ensure key objectives and deadlines are achieved. The role leads coding and audits review activities, including medical record reviews to support accurate risk adjustment revenue, compliance, audits of provider and vendor documentation to ensure accuracy and completeness, and operational readiness efforts for government audits related to risk adjustment programs.

What You’ll Do

Lead Medicare Advantage (MA) and ACA Risk Adjustment coding operations, including chart review programs, RADV and HRADV audit readiness, and coding validation activities to ensure accurate risk score capture, regulatory compliance, and revenue optimization. Expert in HCC and HHS risk adjustment methodology.
Manage and develop a team of certified coding professionals (CPCs), providing leadership, oversight, and coaching while driving coding accuracy, quality performance, and operational excellence.
Partner with providers, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver risk adjustment education, ensure vendor performance and compliance, and implement strategies that improve documentation quality and audit outcomes.

How You’ll Do It

Drive the development and documentation of design, requirements and implementation required to support initiatives that align with strategic priorities.
Develop relationships and partner with key resources, both internal and external, to collaborate on the design and ensure all market, member, and provider considerations are factored into the design.
Drive business decision making process to ensure capabilities, systems and processes meet market expectations and that alternate approaches are vetted and explored.
Manage related ongoing program management work to understand what is needed to recommend strategy and solutions, while influencing and steering others to accomplish that strategy across multiple complex programs.
Ensure that appropriate metrics are chosen and that the appropriate measurement, data analysis and evaluation occur for each initiative.
Develop and continually update program or project plans, timelines and deliverables while coordinating multiple sub-processes to expand and/or improve complex programs.
Develop and implement a communication plan in conjunction with leadership and to support initiatives, including status and progress updates.
Stay abreast of changes in the rapidly evolving health care marketplace and in regulatory or quality‑measurement programs.
Performs additional responsibilities consistent with the scope and level of the role, as assigned.

Required Skills & Experience

5+ years of progressive project/program management experience, with 1+ staff, team lead or project lead experience.
Bachelor’s degree; in lieu of a degree, an additional two years of relevant experience beyond the qualifications listed above may be accepted.

Preferred Skills & Experience

Strong knowledge of CMS risk adjustment models (ACA and Medicare Advantage).
Experience with HCC coding, RADV audits, and/or chart review programs preferred.
CPC, CCS or CRC coding certification strongly preferred.
Experience developing or supporting provider education or training initiatives preferred.
Masters degree in related field.
Ability to communicate expectations and priorities clearly to team members, actively listen to resolve issues and remove barriers, and drive alignment across teams and stakeholders.
Ability to analyze department challenges, guide team decision-making, and collaborate across teams to drive resolution and next steps.
Ability to effectively organize team work, balance priorities across projects, and manage time and resources to ensure timely delivery and coordination.
Healthcare or managed care experience.
Experience managing complex projects which may involve multiple team members, task assignment, working with internal or external clients, managing teams and customer relationships, and managing project deliverables.
Experience in data-driven decision-making.
Process improvement (Lean / Six Sigma) experience.
Familiarity with PM tools & Microsoft analytics tools.

What you will be doing:
1. Security Operations Management
Manage physical security operations across the Bank's branches, offices and other relevant premises, including guarding, CCTV surveillance, access control and alarm monitoring.
Develop and maintain a centralised security management framework, operating procedures and reporting mechanisms to support business and operational requirements.
Ensure the Security Command Centre provides timely monitoring, escalation and response to security incidents.

2. Governance, Policy and Compliance
Own and maintain OCBC Hong Kong physical security policies, standards and procedures in alignment with OCBC Group requirements.
Ensure security operations comply with applicable internal policies, approval authorities, audit requirements and local regulatory expectations.
Coordinate and support internal reviews, audits, control testing and remediation of identified security gaps.

3. Physical Security Risk Management
Conduct or coordinate periodic physical security assessments, including threat and vulnerability risk assessments, for branches, offices and critical facilities.
Review security risks associated with new premises, renovation projects, relocation exercises and changes in business operations, and recommend appropriate controls.
Provide physical security advisory support to business units and review risk acceptance or control exceptions in accordance with established governance.

4. Incident, Crisis and Operational Resilience
Lead or support the response, investigation, escalation and reporting of physical security incidents.
Prepare clear incident reports, identify root causes and ensure corrective and preventive actions are tracked to completion.
Support crisis management, business continuity and operational resilience planning, including emergency drills and scenario exercises relating to physical security threats.

5. Projects and Workplace Transformation
Work closely with Property Services, project teams, building management and business representatives to define and deliver physical security requirements for office and branch projects.
Support Project Helix, OCC Tower and other workplace transformation, relocation, fit-out or renovation initiatives by establishing security design requirements and ensuring proper testing, commissioning and handover.
Organise project and stakeholder meetings to confirm operational requirements, resolve security issues and monitor implementation progress.

Drive appropriate technology upgrades, system integration and process digitalisation to strengthen monitoring capability, reliability and operational efficiency.
Maintain appropriate system documentation, access administration, testing records and business continuity arrangements for critical security systems.

Manage security guarding providers, system vendors and other third-party security service providers, including service performance, contract governance and cost control.
Define and monitor service levels and key performance indicators, and ensure timely remediation of service deficiencies.
Assess the adequacy of third-party physical security controls and ensure compliance with the Bank's security and vendor-management requirements.

Monitor the physical security threat landscape and recommend proportionate improvements to security controls, processes and services.
Prepare management information, performance reports, risk updates and recommendations for senior management and relevant governance forums.
Perform ad-hoc assignments and projects as required.

Degree or professional qualification in security management, risk management, facilities management, engineering or related discipline.
Relevant experience in physical security operations, preferably within banking, financial services, a regulated environment or a large multi-site organisation.
Practical experience in CCTV, access control, guarding operations, incident management, security risk assessment and vendor management.

About our team

We are a dynamic, dedicated team that provides management and support for a global guarding services account that spans across countries. About the role

The Senior Threat Intelligence Analyst supports security and risk decisions across one Of the world's largest cloud and technology environments. We identify, assess, and communicate threats, vulnerabilities, and emerging risks that could impact critical infrastructure, personnel, operations, supply chains, and strategic business initiatives. The successful candidate will operate at the intersection of intelligence collection, investigations, risk management technical analysis, and stakeholder engagement. This is not a traditional security operations or monitoring role. We are seeking an individual who can independently identify leads, develop investigative hypotheses, conduct collection activities, analyze complex information, and drive issues to resolution through persistence, curiosity, and critical thinking.

What you'll do

This role provides the opportunity to work on complex, high-impact security challenges within a global technology environment supporting some of the world's most advanced cloud and Al initiatives. Analysts are exposed to a wide range of missions including intelligence collection, investigations, insider threat supply chain risk, emerging technologies, strategic vulnerability assessments, and geopolitical risk analysis. Team members regularly collaborate with experienced professionals across intelligence, cybersecurity, engineering, investigations, legal, compliance, risk management and physical security disciplines. This position offers exceptional opportunities for professional growth, technical development cross-functional engagement, and exposure to some of the most challenging security and intelligence problems in the industry.

What you need to apply

We're seeking a senior threat intelligence professional With 10+ years Of experience in threat intelligence, intelligence analysis, investigative research and significant experience open-source intelligence (OSINT) collection and analysis. A strong understanding Of the intelligence lifecycle, collection management source evaluation, and structured analysis is important along with the ability to quickly learn new tools and technical environments. You should be curious, persistent and comfortable working independently, with demonstrated ability to identify and pursue leads, question assumptions, identify information gaps, develop investigative hypotheses, and answer complex questions using multiple sources of information. Strong critical thinking and analytical skills with the ability to identify connections, patterns, anomalies, vulnerabilities, and emerging risks.

You should be able to plan and manage intelligence collection across a range of platforms and sources, assess credibility, validate findings, and turn complex information into clear, practical recommendations. You should also be comfortable using Python KQL, SQL, PowerShell, or similar tools to analyze data, identify patterns and anomalies, and support technical investigations. Experience with managed attribution data visualization, analytics, or data management is helpful, as is a background in cyber threat intelligence, counterintelligence, insider threat, investigations, supply chain risk, data analytics or engineering, critical infrastructure security, or geopolitical risk. You'll succeed in this role by taking ownership, using sound judgment, recognizing risks early, communicating actionable intelligence, and building trusted relationships across technical,
operational, investigative, and leadership teams.

What you'll get

We Offer more than just a job we Offer the chance to be part Of a supportive, collaborative team where your growth and contributions truly matter. In this role, you'll thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment While working on a prestigious multinational client account giving you first-hand exposure to global operations and cross-regional collaboration Beyond day-to-day, you'll enjoy opportunities to travel both locally and internationally. We're committed to employee development with access to continuous learning, training programs, and career growth pathways designed to help you succeed and advance. We believe great work deserves great rewards—and we're committed to staying competitive. This role offers a competitive salary and great benefits too. We invest in you so you can thrive—at work and beyond.

The extra stuff

Candidates must be at least 18 years old, legally authorized to work in the job location, and willing to complete the company's pre-employment screening, including a background check and drug screening. This role may require evening, overnight, or weekend work, particularly during emergencies or high-priority events. Work may occur in outdoor or inclement weather or environments requiring protective gear and heightened safety awareness. The role requires the physical ability to sit stand, walk, climb stairs, and occasionally lift up to 25 pounds (11 kg).

This standardized global job description is intended to define the Core responsibilities and requirements Of the Sr. Threat Intelligence Analyst role across regions. new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Inference
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic’s Inference organization serves Claude to millions of users and enterprise customers, across our own products and the world’s largest cloud platforms, with the speed, reliability, and efficiency that frontier AI demands. The stack that makes this possible is deep and tightly coupled: accelerator kernels, an in-house inference engine that manages the entire token path for both production and research workloads, distributed routing, autoscaling, and capacity management. Every layer affects the others, often in ways that are hard to see in isolation. We build across GPUs, TPUs, and Trainium, and the complexity of building, testing, and shipping inference software grows with every platform we add.

We're Looking For a Technical Program Manager To Drive The Programs That Scale It. The Work Spans Four Closely Coupled Areas

Scaling and infrastructure. Routing, autoscaling, and capacity management for the serving fleet, and bringing new capacity online.
Velocity. The toolchains, development environments, and CI/CD that let inference engineers build, test, and ship across every accelerator platform.
Inference engine. The software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer that serves every request.
Performance. Improving throughput, latency, cost, and reliability across the stack, with correctness treated as part of performance.

This is not a status-tracking role. You'll own outcomes end to end, often where no single team is accountable for the whole picture. Much of your value comes from crossing boundaries into Research, Safeguards, Security, Compute, Infrastructure, API, and our cloud and silicon partners, and bringing back the requirements and dependencies that no team sees from inside its own space. There is little process to inherit, and we want to keep it that way: you'll build the minimum machinery the work needs and remove it when it stops helping. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator. We expect TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management and fleet operations can look like.

Key Responsibilities

Own the programs that scale Claude’s serving fleet across accelerator and cloud platforms, from early direction through delivery.
Drive new capacity online end to end, working across compute, infrastructure, security, networking, and inference teams so one person is accountable for the whole path.
Build visibility into supply, demand, and utilization with capacity and finance partners, and drive trade-offs among utilization, cost, latency, and reliability to a clear decision.
Lead reliability programs and large migrations without disrupting production traffic or research, and make sure incident follow-ups land in team roadmaps.
Drive the programs that make inference engineers faster: define the productivity metrics that matter, find the bottlenecks, and improve how software is built, tested, and released across platforms, in step with Anthropic’s central Infrastructure org.
Coordinate roadmaps and priorities across the production, research, and safeguards needs that depend on the same teams.
Track performance and efficiency work from opportunity to measured impact in production, with correctness held as a release criterion.
Own inference readiness for model launches alongside our launch TPMs.

Minimum Qualifications

7+ years of experience as a TPM, or in an equivalent engineering or SRE lead role, owning large multi-team infrastructure programs end to end in production distributed systems, ML infrastructure, or cloud platforms. You can speak to the outcomes in detail, including where a program slipped and what you did about it.
Technical fluency in large-scale serving infrastructure, including request routing and load balancing, autoscaling, capacity planning, cluster orchestration, deployment and rollout, and observability. You know enough to challenge a design, find the real risk, and add value beyond tracking.
A working understanding of how LLM inference uses hardware (prefill and decode, batching, caching, compute versus memory bandwidth versus interconnect), or a track record of getting deep in an unfamiliar technical domain quickly.
A track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on ambiguous, fast-moving efforts, and of retiring process that has stopped earning its keep.
The ability to drive outcomes across organizations you don't manage, with competing priorities and unclear decision ownership. You read people and rooms well, know when to push and when to listen, and earn the trust of senior engineers and researchers.
Strong written communication, including plans, reviews, and executive updates that many teams depend on.
Low ego and high ownership. You do whatever the program needs, whether that is writing a script, running an incident bridge, or chasing a quota, and you care more about the outcome than about scope or credit.
Care about Anthropic's mission and about serving frontier AI safely and reliably.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience with LLM or ML inference serving at scale, such as model servers, batching and scheduling, KV caching, quantization, speculative decoding, or multi-model routing.
Experience with accelerator infrastructure (GPU, TPU, or Trainium), including cluster bring-up, hardware qualification, or running one workload across more than one accelerator platform.
Experience managing capacity across multiple clouds or regions, including demand forecasting, headroom policy, cost modeling, or unit economics for compute-heavy services.
Experience with developer productivity, release engineering, or CI/CD at scale, especially for hardware-dependent workloads, and with using engineering metrics to measurably raise velocity.
Experience running performance or efficiency programs, with enough grounding in rooflines, kernels, ML compilers (XLA, Triton, Neuron), numerics, or collective communication to reason about trade-offs with the engineers doing the work.
Familiarity with Kubernetes-based orchestration and job scheduling.
Experience working with research teams and turning their needs into infrastructure requirements.
Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, including building automations or agents, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$290,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Uphold and advocate for design quality with cross-functional teams and vendors to exceed engagement and registration goals
Inspire and sustain a culture of excellence by collaborating with creatives in best practices and processes

Who you are

Staff Program Managers within Brand Studio at Stripe demonstrate passion for great design and have strong design sense. They’re experts in diving deep into details, expanding, evolving, defining, and documenting flexible systems and processes that achieve bar-raising quality and consistency at scale.

The ideal candidate excels at keeping the work on track while maintaining (and raising) the bar on craft. They offer options and tradeoffs, crisply articulate decisions, iterate quickly, and collaborate seamlessly with senior leadership, marketers, creatives, and agency partners. Most importantly, they are meticulous when it comes to details.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in similar roles and industries
Think users first—understand their needs, find interesting and unique solutions, and strive to consistently optimize how to best engage with them
Have a strong strategic acumen for developing complex program roadmaps and cross-functional processes in a fast-paced environment
Can demonstrate strong design sense, industry knowledge and best practices, have deep knowledge producing complex brand and event design systems, and bringing design assets to life across the creative production process
Proven excellence in producing creative systems that are optimized for scale and growth
Highly detail oriented and excel at simplifying complexity
Strong track record successfully influencing outcomes both internally and with agency partners
Can balance optimizing for speed and quality, with high craft and quality creative work
Are persuasive in explaining your work, process, and decisions
Excellent organization and presentation skills, and excel in written and verbal communication
Are passionate about Stripe’s mission

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $184,000 - $276,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.
